Elena — congrats and thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a working draft of the MAP (v1) with an implementation timeline and an evaluation plan baked into each phase. Key highlights up front:

- Phase 0 (Prep, week 0): credentialing, KMS key exchange, network allowlists, shared testing bucket
- Phase 1 (Canary, week 1): 2-day canary with 5% traffic; primary metrics: 95p latency, 99% success rate for format-preserving responses, token-throughput target 12k tokens/min dedicated pool
- Phase 2 (Incremental migration, weeks 2-3): 25% -> 50% increments with automated fallback policy to hosted variant
- Phase 3 (Full cutover + training, week 4): final ramp, handoff, and two 90-min training sessions for ops/support

Evaluation plan (section 3 in attached evaluation_plan_v1.md):
- Testset: 1,200 prompts capturing our common intents + 150 edge-case prompts for hallucination/regression checks
- Metrics: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token-cost delta, top-1 fidelity (labelled), BERTScore for NLU outputs where applicable
- Regression threshold: any model variant showing >6% degradation in top-1 fidelity or a 30% increase in p95 latency triggers rollback

I've called out internal owners in the MAP and included a mutual action checklist for VitalMesh and Redwood owners. Please review the timeline in the attached spreadsheet and flag any constraints.

Attachments: vitalmesh_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), evaluation_plan_v1.md (markdown), acceptance_criteria.docx (docx)

Next steps / asks for VitalMesh before we schedule the canary:
1) Confirm preferred canary window(s) — weekend vs early-morning weekday
2) Provide a list of ops contacts for training invites (we will send calendar invites once windows are confirmed)
3) Share any compliance test cases you require included in the eval set

Ben/Laura/Marissa — I assigned the canary orchestration, evaluation test authoring, and training respectively in the map; please check your timelines and call out conflicts.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Elena — quick note on the canary and evaluation mechanics from the runtime side. I pulled a concrete cadence into the MAP (see sheet "Canary Schedule"):

- Canary window options (pick one):
  * Option A: Sat 02 Jul 02:00 - 06:00 PT (4 hours; lower business traffic)
  * Option B: Sun 03 Jul 03:00 - 07:00 PT (4 hours)
  * Option C: Tue 05 Jul 01:00 - 05:00 PT (weekday early window; we can throttle)

- Canary controls: 5% traffic for first 2 hours, escalate to 10% for remaining 2 hours if no regressions
- Evaluation checkpoints: automatic evaluation run at t+1h and t+4h (1000-sample smoke test against your provided testset)
- Rollback triggers: any of the following — p95 latency > 1.6x baseline, error-rate > 1.5% absolute, fidelity drop > 6%

Migration plan (minimal disruption strategy):
- We will use sidecar routing to send a copy of requests to the canary variant (mirror mode) during the morning dry-run on Thu 07 Jul to collect telemetry; no user-facing changes
- Live traffic shift will occur only after both evaluation checkpoints pass and your sign-off

Training logistics: Marissa, can you confirm trainer availability week of Jul 12 and your preferred timezone (PT/ET)? I can support a deep-dive on canary ops for our shared runbook.

Elena — can you confirm which option looks best for your Ops team? Also please share the contact for your SRE who will need the traffic-allowlist.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Implementation Engineer
Redwood Inference
